statements: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Al-Ikhlas has six ayahs.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs. Al-Kawthar, with three, is the shortest surah.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty at the first revelation.
Revelation continued for about twenty-three years.
Revelation continued for about ten years.
medium.explain: Revelation continued for approximately twenty-three years: roughly thirteen in Makkah and ten in Madinah.

statements: The Makkan period lasted about thirteen years.
The Madinan period lasted about ten years.
The Madinan period lasted about twenty years.
medium.explain: The Madinan period ran from the Hijrah in 622 CE to the Prophet's passing in 632 CE — about ten years.

statements: Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.
The Day of Arafah falls on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.
The Day of Arafah falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.
medium.explain: Arafah is 9 Dhul-Hijjah; Eid al-Adha is the following day, the 10th.

statements: Surah Yasin is surah 36.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55.
Surah Al-Mulk is surah 77.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mulk is surah 67. Surah 77 is Al-Mursalat.

statements: Sa'i is performed between Safa and Marwah.
Sa'i consists of seven circuits.
Sa'i is performed around the Ka'bah.
medium.explain: Walking around the Ka'bah is Tawaf. Sa'i is the seven circuits between the hills of Safa and Marwah.

statements: Masjid al-Aqsa was the first qiblah.
The qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah in the Madinan period.
The qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah before the Hijrah.
medium.explain: The change of qiblah took place after the Hijrah, during the Madinan period, and is referred to in Surah Al-Baqarah.

statements: Abu Bakr was given the title as-Siddiq.
Umar ibn al-Khattab was given the title al-Faruq.
Uthman ibn Affan was given the title al-Faruq.
medium.explain: Al-Faruq was the title of Umar. Uthman is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

statements: Surah At-Tawbah does not open with the Basmalah.
Surah At-Tawbah is a Madinan surah.
Surah At-Tawbah is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: At-Tawbah has 129 ayahs and is one of the longer surahs. The shortest is Al-Kawthar.

statements: There are six articles of faith.
There are five pillars of Islam.
There are six pillars of Islam.
medium.explain: There are five pillars of Islam and six articles of iman. The six is the articles of faith, not the pillars.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.
Laylat al-Qadr falls on a fixed, known date every year.
medium.explain: Its exact night is not fixed in the sources. It is sought across the last ten nights, most commonly on the odd-numbered ones.

statements: Zakat is commonly 2.5% on qualifying savings.
Zakat becomes due after a lunar year has passed.
Zakat is due on all wealth, with no minimum threshold.
medium.explain: Zakat is due only on wealth above the nisab threshold. Below it, no zakat is owed.

statements: The Hijri calendar is lunar.
The Hijri year is shorter than the Gregorian year.
The Hijri year is longer than the Gregorian year.
medium.explain: A lunar year is roughly 354 days, about eleven days shorter than the Gregorian year — which is why Ramadan moves earlier each year.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of the people of the cave.
Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of Dhul-Qarnayn.
Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of Yusuf.
medium.explain: The story of Yusuf is told in Surah Yusuf (12). Al-Kahf contains the cave sleepers, the two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

statements: Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Luqman is surah 31.
Surah Yusuf is surah 10.
medium.explain: Surah Yusuf is surah 12. Surah 10 is Yunus.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty when revelation began.
He lived about twenty-three years after that.
He lived about forty years after that.
medium.explain: Revelation lasted about twenty-three years, and the Prophet ﷺ was around sixty-three at his passing.

statements: Khadijah was the first to believe in the Prophet's message.
Khadijah died before the Hijrah.
Khadijah died after the conquest of Makkah.
medium.explain: Khadijah died around 619 CE in the Year of Sorrow, some three years before the Hijrah and eleven before the conquest of Makkah.

statements: Zakat is due once a lunar year has passed on qualifying wealth.
The nisab is the minimum threshold for zakat.
The nisab is the rate at which zakat is paid.
medium.explain: The nisab is the threshold of wealth; the rate on most savings is 2.5%.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas is about the oneness of Allah.
Surah Al-Kafirun addresses the disbelievers of Makkah.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is the longest surah in juz 30.
medium.explain: Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs and is among the shortest. The longest surah in juz 30 is An-Naba, with forty.

statements: The Ansar were from Madinah.
The Muhajirun emigrated from Makkah.
The Ansar emigrated from Makkah.
medium.explain: The Ansar were the helpers of Madinah who received the Muhajirun, the emigrants from Makkah.

statements: Tarawih is prayed in Ramadan.
Tahajjud is prayed after sleeping.
Tarawih is prayed before the Isha prayer.
medium.explain: Tarawih follows Isha. It is not prayed before it.

statements: The Qur'an has 30 ajza.
Juz 30 is called Juz Amma.
Juz 1 is called Juz Amma.
medium.explain: Juz Amma is the thirtieth, named after the opening words of Surah An-Naba, 'Amma yatasa'alun'.

statements: Sa'i is performed seven times between Safa and Marwah.
Tawaf is seven circuits of the Ka'bah.
Sa'i is performed three times.
medium.explain: Both Tawaf and Sa'i consist of seven, not three.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ had a daughter named Fatimah.
Fatimah married Ali ibn Abi Talib.
Fatimah married Uthman ibn Affan.
medium.explain: Fatimah married Ali ibn Abi Talib. Uthman married two of the Prophet's other daughters in succession, which is why he is called Dhun-Nurayn.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah contains Ayat al-Kursi.
Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255.
Ayat al-Kursi is a complete surah.
medium.explain: Ayat al-Kursi is a single verse within Surah Al-Baqarah, not a surah in its own right.

statements: The Hijri year has twelve months.
The Hijri calendar follows the moon.
The Hijri calendar follows the sun.
medium.explain: The Hijri calendar is lunar, which is why its months shift relative to the solar seasons.

statements: Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph.
Umar accepted Islam in Makkah before the Hijrah.
Umar was the first caliph.
medium.explain: Abu Bakr was the first caliph; Umar succeeded him in 13 AH.

statements: Isa is called al-Masih in the Qur'an.
The Qur'an says Isa was raised up rather than killed.
The Qur'an says Isa was the son of Allah.
medium.explain: The Qur'an explicitly rejects this, affirming that Isa is a servant and messenger of Allah.

statements: The first qiblah was Jerusalem.
The qiblah changed to the Ka'bah.
The qiblah changed from the Ka'bah to Jerusalem.
medium.explain: The change ran the other way: from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah, during the Madinan period.

statements: Hajj has a fixed season.
Ihram is entered at a boundary called the miqat.
Ihram may be entered at any point, including inside Makkah, for Hajj from outside.
medium.explain: Those coming from outside enter ihram at the designated miqat before crossing into the sacred precinct.

statements: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah.
They sheltered in the cave of Thawr.
They sheltered in the cave of Hira.
medium.explain: Hira is where the first revelation came, before the Hijrah. The cave on the migration journey was Thawr.

statements: A hadith has a chain of narrators and a text.
The chain is called the isnad.
The chain is called the matn.
medium.explain: The isnad is the chain of narrators; the matn is the text of the report.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is called Umm al-Kitab.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the longest surah.
medium.explain: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs. Al-Baqarah, with 286, is the longest.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah is surah 56.
Surah Al-Hadid is surah 57.
Surah Al-Mujadilah is surah 59.
medium.explain: Al-Mujadilah is surah 58. Surah 59 is Al-Hashr.

statements: Ghusl is the full washing of the body.
Wudu is the partial ablution.
Ghusl is required before every prayer.
medium.explain: Wudu is required before prayer. Ghusl is obligatory only in specific states.

statements: The Battle of the Camel was fought in Ali's caliphate.
Siffin was fought in Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of the Camel was fought in the Prophet's lifetime.
medium.explain: Both battles belong to the first fitnah, after the Prophet's passing, during Ali's caliphate.

statements: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn are Al-Falaq and An-Nas.
Both begin with 'Qul a'udhu'.
Al-Mu'awwidhatayn are Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq.
medium.explain: The two surahs of seeking refuge are Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114). Al-Ikhlas precedes them.

statements: Juz 29 begins with Surah Al-Mulk.
Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
Juz 29 begins with Surah An-Naba.
medium.explain: An-Naba opens juz 30. Juz 29 begins with Al-Mulk.

statements: The miqat is where pilgrims enter ihram.
There are several mawaqit in different directions.
The miqat is the plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th.
medium.explain: That plain is Arafah. The mawaqit are boundary points where ihram is entered.

statements: Ramy al-Jamarat takes place at Mina.
Tawaf takes place at the Masjid al-Haram.
Ramy al-Jamarat takes place at Arafah.

It is a Makkan surah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Jumu'ah is Madinan, as the Friday congregational prayer was established in Madinah.

statements: Taqwa is often rendered as God-consciousness.
Surah Al-Hujurat says the most honoured have the most taqwa.

medium.explain: Al-Hujurat 49:13 states the opposite: honour lies in taqwa, not lineage.

statements: Shirk is associating partners with Allah.
Tawhid is the oneness of Allah.
Shirk and tawhid mean the same thing.
medium.explain: They are direct opposites: tawhid affirms oneness, shirk violates it.

statements: Surah An-Naba has 40 ayahs.
Surah An-Naba opens juz 30.
Surah An-Naba is a Madinan surah.
medium.explain: Surah An-Naba is Makkan, like most of juz 30.

statements: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was among the ten promised Paradise.

Umar appointed a council of ten to choose his successor.

statements: Sabr means patience.

Sabr means gratitude.

statements: Surah Al-Hadid is named after iron.

It is named after a prophet.
medium.explain: Al-Hadid means 'the iron'. It is not named after a person.

statements: The Hijri calendar has twelve months.
Its first month is Muharram.
Its first month is Ramadan.
medium.explain: The year begins with Muharram. Ramadan is the ninth month.

statements: Umm Salamah had migrated to Abyssinia.
She gave decisive counsel at Hudaybiyyah.
She was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ.
medium.explain: Khadijah was the Prophet's first wife. Umm Salamah married him in Madinah after the death of her husband Abu Salamah.

statements: Ikhlas means sincerity of intention.
Actions are judged by intentions, per a well-known hadith.
Ikhlas means patience in hardship.
medium.explain: Patience is sabr. Ikhlas is doing an act purely for Allah.

statements: Surah Al-Mujadilah concerns a woman who argued her case.
It is surah 58.
It concerns a woman who led an army.
medium.explain: The surah is named for the woman who disputed with the Prophet ﷺ concerning her husband.

statements: Zakat is due after a lunar year on qualifying wealth.
The nisab is the minimum threshold.
Zakat is due immediately on receiving any income.
medium.explain: Zakat on wealth requires a lunar year to pass over holdings above the nisab.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf has four main stories.
One concerns Musa and al-Khidr.
One concerns Yusuf and his brothers.
medium.explain: The story of Yusuf is in Surah Yusuf. Al-Kahf contains the cave sleepers, the two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf has 101 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs, the same count as Al-Isra. Al-Kahf has 110.

Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
Juz 30 contains 36 surahs.
hard.explain: Juz 30 runs from Surah An-Naba (78) to An-Nas (114), which is 37 surahs, not 36.

Surah Al-Muddaththir came early, after the pause in revelation.
Surah Al-Fatihah was the first revelation.
hard.explain: The first revelation was Surah Al-Alaq, verses 1–5, at the cave of Hira. Al-Fatihah was revealed early in the Makkan period but was not the first.

Surah Ar-Rahman is part of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Its refrain is repeated 31 times.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH.

Umar's caliphate lasted roughly two years.

statements: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not open with the Basmalah.
The Basmalah appears within Surah An-Naml.

Surah Ta-Ha is surah 20.
Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 20.

statements: Mu'tah was fought in 8 AH.

hard.explain: Surah An-Nasr has three ayahs, like Al-Kawthar and Al-Asr.

Surah Quraysh precedes Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.

statements: Surah Yusuf tells one continuous narrative.
Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf is Makkan. It has 111 ayahs and is distinctive for telling a single sustained narrative.

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj died in 875 CE.
Abu Dawud compiled one of the two Sahih collections.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman's refrain appears 31 times.
Surah Al-Mursalat also has a repeated refrain.
Surah Ar-Rahman is a surah of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Al-Mursalat does have its own repeated refrain.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijrah took place in the month of Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijri calendar begins its year with Rabi al-Awwal.
hard.explain: The Hijri year begins with Muharram. The calendar counts from the year of the Hijrah, but its first month is Muharram, not the month of the migration itself.

statements: Surah Al-Isra is also known as Bani Isra'il.
Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Al-Isra is also known as Surah Al-Mi'raj.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Isra (17) is also called Bani Isra'il. 'Surah Al-Mi'raj' is not one of its recognised names.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is surah 18.
Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 19.
hard.explain: Ta-Ha is surah 20, immediately after Maryam.

statements: Surah Al-Hajj contains a sajdah.
Surah As-Sajdah contains a sajdah.

statements: Khaybar was in 7 AH.

Al-Tirmidhi died in 892 CE.
Al-Nasa'i died before al-Tirmidhi.

statements: Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs.
Surah Al-Anfal has 120 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs.

The Battle of the Camel was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of Siffin was fought during Uthman's caliphate.

statements: Surah Al-Fath was revealed in connection with Hudaybiyyah.
Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah Al-Hashr relates largely to Badr.

statements: Surah Yunus is surah 10.
Surah Hud is surah 11.
Surah Ibrahim is surah 13.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled a Musnad.
Al-Shafi'i compiled the Muwatta.

statements: The Hijri calendar was formally instituted during Umar's caliphate.
Its first year corresponds to 622 CE.
It was formally instituted during Abu Bakr's caliphate.
hard.explain: The calendar was formally established under Umar, who set its starting point at the year of the Hijrah.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah is surah 56.
Surah Al-Hadid is surah 57.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 56.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55, immediately before Al-Waqi'ah.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit led the compilation under Abu Bakr.

statements: Surah Al-Mulk has 30 ayahs.
Surah Nuh has 28 ayahs.
Surah Al-Jinn has 18 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Jinn has 28 ayahs. Surah Al-Jinn and Surah Nuh both have 28.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant by the traditional account.

hard.explain: The traditional account places the first revelation at about the age of forty.

statements: Surah Al-Ankabut is surah 29.
Surah Ar-Rum is surah 30.
Surah As-Sajdah is surah 31.
hard.explain: As-Sajdah is surah 32. Surah 31 is Luqman.

statements: Abu Hanifah is associated with Kufa.
Malik ibn Anas is associated with Madinah.

statements: Surah Al-Qadr describes a night better than a thousand months.
Surah Al-Qadr has five ayahs.
Surah Al-Qadr is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qadr (97) is generally classified as Makkan, though a minority view holds otherwise.

statements: Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 10 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 9 AH.

statements: Surah Al-Fil has five ayahs.
Surah Quraysh has four ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'un has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'un has seven ayahs.

It contains the verse naming the Prophet ﷺ the seal of the prophets.
It is a Makkan surah.

statements: Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah At-Tawbah follows it in the mushaf.
Surah Al-Anfal has 129 ayahs.
hard.explain: Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs. It is At-Tawbah that has 129.

statements: Surah Qaf is surah 50.
Surah Sad is surah 38.
Surah Nun is the common name of surah 67.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qalam, which opens with the letter Nun, is surah 68. Surah 67 is Al-Mulk.

statements: Al-Sab' al-Tiwal begins with Al-Baqarah.

It consists of nine surahs.
hard.explain: The name means 'the seven long ones'. The dispute concerns which surah occupies the seventh place.

statements: Ibn Khaldun wrote the Muqaddimah.
He died in 1406 CE.
He wrote Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim.
hard.explain: That tafsir is Ibn Kathir's. Ibn Khaldun is known for the Muqaddimah and his universal history.

statements: Surah Al-Mumtahanah is surah 60.
Surah As-Saff is surah 61.
Surah Al-Hashr is surah 61.
hard.explain: Al-Hashr is surah 59. As-Saff is 61.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit was of the Ansar.
He led the compilation under Abu Bakr.
He was among the Muhajirun.

Zayd compiles the Qur'an under Abu Bakr
Zayd leads the standardisation under Uthman

hard.explain: Zayd ibn Thabit's role in the preservation of the Qur'an, from scribe to the two great compilations.

events.text: Aisha is present at the Battle of the Camel

hard.explain: Aisha's life after the Hijrah. Surah An-Nur was revealed in connection with the slander against her, and she became one of the foremost narrators of hadith.
The two grandsons of the Prophet ﷺ, from their births in Madinah to Karbala.

events.text: Abu Hurayrah serves as governor of Bahrain

hard.explain: Abu Hurayrah accepted Islam around the time of Khaybar and, in a few years of companionship, became the most prolific narrator of hadith.

events.text: Uthman is sent as envoy to Makkah at Hudaybiyyah

hard.explain: Uthman ibn Affan's life. The rumour of his death as envoy at Hudaybiyyah prompted the Pledge of Ridwan.

events.text: The trench is dug at Khandaq
Salman serves as governor of Mada'in

hard.explain: Salman al-Farisi, originally from Persia, whose suggestion of the trench shaped the defence of Madinah.

easy.set: The five pillars of Islam
easy.explain: The five pillars are the shahada (testimony of faith), salah (prayer), zakat (obligatory charity), sawm (fasting Ramadan), and Hajj for those able.

easy.set: The five daily prayers
easy.explain: The five obligatory prayers in order through the day: Fajr before sunrise, Dhuhr after midday, Asr in the afternoon, Maghrib after sunset, and Isha at night.

easy.set: The four Rashidun caliphs
easy.explain: The four rightly-guided caliphs, in order: Abu Bakr, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan, and Ali ibn Abi Talib.

easy.set: The first four surahs of the Qur'an
easy.explain: The Qur'an opens with Al-Fatihah, followed by the three long surahs Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran and An-Nisa.

easy.set: The last three surahs of the Qur'an
easy.explain: The Qur'an closes with Al-Ikhlas (112), Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114). The last two together are known as al-Mu'awwidhatayn.

easy.set: The first four prayers of the day, in order
easy.explain: The day's prayers in order are Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. These are the first four.

easy.set: The two Eids and the month each falls in
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal and Eid al-Adha on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.

easy.set: The four archangels commonly named in Islamic teaching
easy.explain: Jibril brings revelation, Mika'il is associated with provision and rain, Israfil with the trumpet, and Malak al-Mawt with death. Malik, Munkar and Nakir are angels with other roles.

easy.set: The first five surahs of the Qur'an
easy.explain: The mushaf opens with Al-Fatihah, followed by the long surahs Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa and Al-Ma'idah.

easy.set: The last four surahs of the Qur'an
easy.explain: The final four are Al-Masad (111), Al-Ikhlas (112), Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114).

easy.set: The two meals connected with fasting, and their times
easy.explain: Suhur is eaten before dawn, before the fast begins; iftar breaks the fast at sunset.

easy.set: The three holiest mosques in Islam
easy.explain: The three mosques to which travel is specifically encouraged are the Masjid al-Haram in Makkah, the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, and Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem.

easy.set: The parts of the body washed in wudu
easy.explain: The Qur'an specifies washing the face and the arms to the elbows, wiping the head, and washing the feet to the ankles.

easy.set: The five pillars, in their usual order
easy.explain: The usual order is the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat, fasting Ramadan, and Hajj for those able.

easy.set: The main positions of a rak'ah, in order
easy.explain: A unit of prayer moves from standing (qiyam) to bowing (ruku'), then prostration, a brief sitting, and a second prostration.

easy.set: The five daily prayers and their rak'ah counts
easy.explain: The obligatory rak'ah counts are Fajr two, Dhuhr four, Asr four, Maghrib three and Isha four.

easy.set: The three Ulul-Azm prophets before Musa
easy.explain: In the traditional ordering the five of firm resolve are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ. These are the first three.

easy.set: The four months of the Islamic year that follow Ramadan
easy.explain: Ramadan is the ninth month, followed by Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah, after which a new year begins with Muharram.

easy.set: The prophets given the Tawrat, Zabur, Injil and Qur'an
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to Isa, and the Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ. Ibrahim received the Suhuf.

easy.set: Five surahs of juz 30, in order
easy.explain: Surahs 109 to 113 in order. An-Nas, surah 114, comes immediately after.

easy.set: The first four of the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah leading to Arafah
easy.explain: Pilgrims move to Mina on the 8th and stand at Arafah on the 9th, with Eid al-Adha on the 10th.

easy.set: The words of the first part of the shahada, in order
easy.explain: The first part of the testimony is 'La ilaha illa Allah' — there is no god but Allah. The second affirms that Muhammad is His Messenger.

easy.set: The two angels named in the Qur'an, and two more named in hadith
easy.explain: Jibril and Mika'il are named in the Qur'an. Israfil and Malik, the keeper of the Fire, are known from other sources; Harut and Marut are mentioned in Al-Baqarah but are a separate matter.

easy.set: The four prophets with a surah named after them, in mushaf order
easy.explain: These are surahs 10, 11, 12 and 14. Surah Muhammad (47) and Surah Nuh (71) come much later in the mushaf.

easy.set: The main acts of Umrah, in order
easy.explain: Umrah consists of entering ihram, Tawaf, Sa'i, then shaving or shortening the hair. The decoys are rites belonging to Hajj alone.

easy.set: Four of the six articles of faith
easy.explain: The six articles are Allah, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.

easy.set: The first four verses of Surah Al-Ikhlas, by theme
items: He neither begets nor is born
Nor is there to Him any equivalent
decoys: All praise is due to Allah
Master of the Day of Judgement
Guide us to the straight path
easy.explain: Surah Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs declaring the absolute oneness of Allah. The decoys are from Surah Al-Fatihah.

easy.set: The three parts of a complete prostration cycle
easy.explain: Each rak'ah contains two prostrations separated by a brief sitting.

easy.set: Four prophets who are sons or grandsons of Ibrahim
easy.explain: Isma'il and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim, Ya'qub was his grandson through Ishaq, and Yusuf was Ya'qub's son.

easy.set: The three things the Prophet ﷺ was asked about in the Hadith of Jibril
easy.explain: Jibril asked about Islam, Iman and Ihsan in turn, and then about the signs of the Hour.

easy.set: Surahs 109 to 112, in order
easy.explain: Surahs 109 to 112. Al-Falaq and An-Nas follow immediately after.

easy.set: Surahs 105 to 108, in order
easy.explain: Surahs 105 to 108. Al-Kafirun, surah 109, comes next.

easy.set: The four prophets in the line of Ibrahim through Ishaq
easy.explain: Ishaq was Ibrahim's son, Ya'qub his son, and Yusuf his son in turn. Isma'il was Ibrahim's other son, from whom a different line descends.

easy.set: The three prayers with four rak'ahs
easy.explain: Dhuhr, Asr and Isha each have four obligatory rak'ahs. Fajr has two and Maghrib three.

easy.set: The months in which the two Eids fall, and the two around them
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr falls at the start of Shawwal after Ramadan, and Eid al-Adha on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.

easy.set: Four prophets sent to specific named peoples
easy.explain: The Qur'an names the peoples to whom Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb were sent, and describes Yunus and the people of his city.

easy.set: The order of events in a single rak'ah
easy.explain: A rak'ah proceeds from standing recitation, to ruku', to rising, to two prostrations. The tashahhud and salam come at the end of the prayer rather than in every rak'ah.

easy.set: The three stages of the call to Islam in Makkah
easy.explain: The Makkan period moved from private calling, to the public call after about three years, to seeking support in Ta'if and then Yathrib. The decoys belong to the Madinan period.

easy.set: Four well-known companions and what they are best known for
easy.explain: The decoys are scholars of later generations, not companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

easy.set: The three phrases of the tasbih said after the prayer
decoys: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
easy.explain: The well-known tasbih after the obligatory prayer is SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar, commonly counted thirty-three, thirty-three and thirty-four. The decoys are other phrases of remembrance said at other times.

easy.set: The three categories of people the Qur'an opens by describing in Al-Baqarah
easy.explain: The opening passages of Surah Al-Baqarah describe the God-conscious, those who reject, and the hypocrites in turn.

easy.set: Four things forbidden while in ihram
easy.explain: Certain ordinarily permitted acts become prohibited in the state of ihram. The decoys remain entirely permitted.

easy.set: The first four prophets in the traditional list
easy.explain: The conventional ordering of the twenty-five prophets named in the Qur'an begins Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim.

easy.set: The last four prophets in the traditional list
easy.explain: The traditional list ends Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa and finally Muhammad ﷺ, the seal of the prophets.

easy.set: Three acts that are pillars of Islam but not daily
easy.explain: Zakat is annual, fasting is for one month a year, and Hajj is once in a lifetime for those able. Salah is the daily pillar.

easy.set: Surahs 101 to 104, in order
easy.explain: Surahs 101 to 104. Al-Fil is 105, immediately after Al-Humazah.

easy.set: Surahs 97 to 100, in order
easy.explain: Surahs 97 to 100. Al-Alaq is 96 and At-Tin 95, just before; Al-Qari'ah is 101, just after.

easy.set: The three prophets given kingdoms as well as prophethood
easy.explain: Yusuf was given authority in Egypt, and Dawud and Sulayman were given kingdoms. The decoys were prophets without temporal rule.

easy.set: The three prophets connected with Egypt in the Qur'an
easy.explain: Yusuf rose to authority in Egypt, and Musa and his brother Harun were sent to its ruler.

easy.set: The four things Muslims abstain from while fasting
easy.explain: The fast requires abstaining from food, drink and marital relations during daylight hours. Ordinary daily activity continues as normal.

easy.set: Four prophets mentioned as having been tested severely
easy.explain: Each of the four listed faced a well-known trial recounted in the Qur'an. The decoys describe blessings rather than trials.

easy.set: The three parts of the Islamic testimony of faith and action
easy.explain: The Hadith of Jibril explains Islam (outward submission), Iman (belief) and Ihsan (excellence in worship) in turn.

easy.set: Four of the prophets named in the Qur'an beginning with the letter Y
easy.explain: Four of the twenty-five named prophets begin with Y in the usual transliteration. The decoys all begin with I.

easy.set: The three categories of the hereafter mentioned in Surah Al-Waqi'ah
easy.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah divides people into three groups: the foremost, the companions of the right hand, and the companions of the left.

easy.set: Four cities significant in Islamic history
easy.explain: Makkah, Madinah and Jerusalem hold the three holiest mosques, and Damascus was the Umayyad capital.

easy.set: The three prayers recited aloud in congregation
easy.explain: The recitation is aloud in Fajr and in the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and Isha. Dhuhr and Asr are recited quietly.

easy.set: Four companions known for narrating many hadith
easy.explain: The decoys are compilers of hadith from later generations, not companions who narrated them.

easy.set: Four months of the Islamic year, 1st to 4th
easy.explain: The year opens with Muharram, Safar and the two Rabi months.

easy.set: The three things said to continue benefiting a person after death
items: A righteous child who prays for them
easy.explain: A well-known hadith states that when a person dies their deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who supplicates for them.

easy.set: Three acts performed during both Hajj and Umrah
easy.explain: Ihram, Tawaf and Sa'i are common to both. The decoys are rites of Hajj alone.

medium.set: The six articles of faith
medium.explain: The six articles of iman, as listed in the Hadith of Jibril: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.
decoys: Belief in the miracles of the prophets

medium.set: The five Ulul-Azm prophets
medium.explain: The prophets of firm resolve, named together in Surah Al-Ahzab and Surah Ash-Shura: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ.

medium.set: The revealed scriptures named in the Qur'an
medium.explain: The Qur'an names the scrolls of Ibrahim, the Tawrat given to Musa, the Zabur given to Dawud, the Injil given to Isa, and the Qur'an itself.

medium.set: The four sacred months
medium.explain: The four sacred months in which fighting was traditionally forbidden: three consecutive — Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram — and Rajab, which stands alone.

medium.set: The first four months of the Islamic year
medium.explain: The Islamic year begins with Muharram, followed by Safar, Rabi al-Awwal and Rabi al-Thani.

medium.set: The eight categories entitled to zakat, first four
items: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled
medium.explain: Surah At-Tawbah 9:60 names eight categories. The first four are the poor, the needy, the collectors of zakat, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled.

medium.set: The eight categories entitled to zakat, last four
medium.explain: The remaining four categories in Surah At-Tawbah 9:60 are freeing those in bondage, the debt-burdened, in the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveller.

medium.set: The prophets given a revealed scripture
medium.explain: The Qur'an names scriptures given to Ibrahim (the Suhuf), Musa (the Tawrat), Dawud (the Zabur), Isa (the Injil) and Muhammad ﷺ (the Qur'an).

medium.set: The three prophets most often named in the Qur'an
medium.explain: Musa is named far more often than any other prophet, followed by Ibrahim and Nuh. Counts vary slightly by how derived forms are tallied.

medium.set: The four months of the Islamic year containing Ramadan
medium.explain: Ramadan is the ninth month, preceded by Rajab and Sha'ban and followed by Shawwal, in which Eid al-Fitr falls.

medium.set: The rites of Umrah, in order
medium.explain: Umrah consists of entering ihram at the miqat, Tawaf, Sa'i, then shaving or shortening the hair. The decoys listed are rites specific to Hajj.

medium.set: The surahs commonly called al-Mu'awwidhatayn, and the one before them
medium.explain: Al-Falaq and An-Nas together are al-Mu'awwidhatayn, the two surahs of seeking refuge. Al-Ikhlas immediately precedes them.

medium.set: The first four Muslims, as traditionally listed
medium.explain: Khadijah was the first to believe, followed by Abu Bakr among the men, Ali among the young, and Zayd ibn Harithah. The precise ordering after Khadijah is discussed by historians.

medium.set: The three days of Tashriq and the day before them
medium.explain: The Day of Sacrifice is 10 Dhul-Hijjah, followed by the three days of Tashriq on the 11th, 12th and 13th.

medium.set: The stages of Hajj on 8–10 Dhul-Hijjah, in order
medium.explain: Pilgrims go to Mina on the 8th, stand at Arafah on the 9th, spend that night at Muzdalifah, then return to Mina on the 10th for the stoning and the sacrifice.

medium.set: The six articles of faith, in their usual order
medium.explain: The six articles as listed in the Hadith of Jibril. Belief in the jinn is part of Islamic belief but is not one of these six.

medium.set: The ten days of Dhul-Hijjah: the key days in order
medium.explain: Pilgrims travel to Mina on the 8th, stand at Arafah on the 9th, and the 10th is the Day of Sacrifice, followed by the days of Tashriq.

medium.set: The four Rashidun caliphs with their best-known titles
medium.explain: The decoys are genuine titles, but of companions who were not among the four caliphs: Hamza the chief of martyrs, Khalid the sword of Allah, and Abu Ubaydah the trustworthy one of the ummah.

medium.set: The five prayers with their time markers
items: Dhuhr — after the sun passes its zenith
decoys: Tahajjud — last third of the night
medium.explain: The five obligatory prayers each have a defined window. The decoys are voluntary prayers with their own recommended times.

medium.set: The main conditions for zakat to be due
items: The wealth is of a zakatable type
medium.explain: Zakat becomes due on zakatable wealth owned above the nisab once a lunar year has passed over it. Paying in Ramadan is common but not a condition.

medium.set: The four prophets most frequently mentioned after Musa
medium.explain: After Musa, the most frequently named are Ibrahim, Nuh, Lut and Yusuf. The decoys are among the least frequently named. Exact counts vary by how derived forms are tallied.

medium.set: The surahs of juz 30 from An-Naba onward, first four
medium.explain: Juz 30 begins at An-Naba (78) and runs through to An-Nas (114).

medium.set: The three categories of hadith grading most commonly used
medium.explain: Sahih, hasan and da'if are the main grades of reliability. Mawdu means fabricated; mutawatir and ahad classify by number of chains, not reliability.

medium.set: The four main schools and the regions they are most associated with
items: Hanbali — Baghdad and the Arabian peninsula
medium.explain: The four surviving Sunni schools and their historical centres. The decoys include real schools that did not survive as widely followed madhhabs.

medium.set: The acts that invalidate the fast
medium.explain: Eating or drinking forgetfully does not break the fast, according to the great majority of scholars. Scholars differ on some of the other cases listed as decoys.

medium.set: The pillars of the prayer, four of them in order
decoys: Turning the head at the salam
medium.explain: The decoys are recommended or optional acts, not pillars whose omission invalidates the prayer. Schools differ slightly on the precise list of pillars.

medium.set: The four caliphs' years of accession in the Hijri calendar
medium.explain: The Rashidun period ran from 11 AH to 40 AH, after which Umayyad rule was established under Mu'awiyah.

medium.set: The scriptures and their recipients
medium.explain: The five revealed scriptures named in the Qur'an and the prophets who received them. The decoys are books compiled by people, not revelation.

medium.set: The three mosques and the cities they stand in
medium.explain: The three mosques toward which travel is specifically encouraged. The decoys are significant mosques that do not fall under that category.

medium.set: The four things mentioned in Surah Al-Asr as saving mankind from loss
medium.explain: Surah Al-Asr states that mankind is in loss except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and counsel one another to truth and to patience.

medium.set: The main rites of Hajj on the Day of Sacrifice
medium.explain: On 10 Dhul-Hijjah pilgrims stone the largest pillar, offer the sacrifice, shave or shorten, and perform Tawaf al-Ifadah. Scholars permit some variation in the order.

medium.set: Four surahs of juz 29, in order
medium.explain: Juz 29 begins at Al-Mulk (67). The decoys are surahs 71 to 74, which also fall in that juz but later.

medium.set: The prayers that may be shortened when travelling
medium.explain: Only the four-rak'ah prayers may be shortened to two when travelling. Fajr and Maghrib are not shortened.

medium.set: Four of the Prophet's wives
medium.explain: The decoys are daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, not his wives — a distinction worth keeping clear.

medium.set: Four early converts to Islam
medium.explain: The decoys all accepted Islam later: Umar and Hamza during the Makkan period, and Khalid and Amr shortly before the conquest of Makkah.

medium.set: Four surahs commonly recited in the Friday prayer and on Fridays
medium.explain: Al-Kahf is commonly recited on Fridays, and Al-Jumu'ah, Al-A'la and Al-Ghashiyah are reported among those recited in the prayer itself.

medium.set: Four of the Ten Promised Paradise (al-Ashara al-Mubashshara)
medium.explain: The ten named in the well-known narration include the four caliphs, Talhah, Zubayr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa'id ibn Zayd and Abu Ubaydah.

medium.set: Four more of the Ten Promised Paradise
medium.explain: The decoys are eminent companions who are not among the ten named in that particular narration.

medium.set: The conditions of the prayer before it begins
items: Covering the required areas of the body
The time for the prayer having entered
medium.explain: These are conditions that must be met before the prayer is valid. The decoys are recommended or merely customary, not conditions.

medium.set: Four categories of people exempt from fasting, with the remedy
items: The temporarily ill — make up later
medium.explain: The Qur'an exempts the sick and the traveller, who make the days up later. Those permanently unable give fidyah instead. The decoys have no basis.

medium.set: Four well-known works of Islamic scholarship and their authors
medium.explain: The decoys deliberately mismatch well-known books with the wrong authors.

medium.set: The four Jumu'ah requirements commonly agreed on
items: It falls in the time of Dhuhr
It is preceded by a khutbah
decoys: It must be in the largest mosque
It requires forty attendees in all schools
It must be led by a scholar
medium.explain: Jumu'ah is two rak'ahs in the Dhuhr time, in congregation, preceded by the sermon. Schools differ on the minimum number of attendees, so that is not an agreed requirement.

medium.set: Four voluntary prayers and when they are offered
medium.explain: The decoys are obligatory prayers, not voluntary ones.

medium.set: The four things Surah Al-Asr identifies, in order
items: Except those who believe and do good
And counsel each other to truth and patience
medium.explain: Surah Al-Asr is three ayahs: the oath, the declaration of loss, and the exceptions — faith, righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and patience.

medium.set: Four battles of the Madinan period, in order
medium.explain: The decoys all took place after the Prophet's passing, during the Rashidun caliphates.

medium.set: The five obligatory prayers with the number of rak'ahs recited aloud
medium.explain: Recitation is aloud in Fajr and in the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and Isha, and quiet in Dhuhr and Asr. Jumu'ah is recited aloud.

medium.set: Four surahs that open with praise of Allah (al-Hamd)
medium.explain: Five surahs open with 'Alhamdulillah': Al-Fatihah, Al-An'am, Al-Kahf, Saba and Fatir.

medium.set: Four of the Prophet's daughters
medium.explain: The decoys are wives of the Prophet ﷺ rather than daughters.

medium.set: Four companions who served as scribes of revelation
medium.explain: A number of companions wrote down revelation. The decoys were eminent companions known for other roles.

medium.set: Four surahs named after creatures or animals
medium.explain: Several surahs take their names from creatures. Al-Fath is the odd one among the decoys, being named for a victory rather than an animal.

medium.set: The four rightly-guided caliphs and the tribe they shared
medium.explain: All four Rashidun caliphs were of Quraysh. The decoys are companions from outside that lineage, reflecting the diversity of the early community.

medium.set: Four stages of the Qur'an's preservation
medium.explain: The Qur'an was memorised and written during the Prophet's life, gathered into one collection under Abu Bakr, and standardised under Uthman.

medium.set: Four surahs commonly recited for protection
medium.explain: Al-Fatihah, Ayat al-Kursi and the two Mu'awwidhatayn are widely recited for protection. Ayat al-Kursi is a verse rather than a surah.

medium.set: Four terms describing the Qur'an's own divisions
medium.explain: Surah, ayah, juz and hizb are divisions of the Qur'anic text. The decoys are terms from hadith study and exegesis.

medium.set: Four events that took place during Ramadan
medium.explain: Several major events fell in Ramadan, including Badr in 2 AH and the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. The decoys took place in other months.

medium.set: Four of the prohibitions listed in Surah Al-Hujurat
medium.explain: Surah Al-Hujurat prohibits mockery, offensive nicknames, suspicion, spying and backbiting.

medium.set: Four companions appointed as governors or commanders
medium.explain: These four held significant appointments. The decoys pair real companions with posts they did not hold.

medium.set: The four main categories of water purity discussed by jurists
medium.explain: Jurists classify water by its purity and its capacity to purify. The decoys describe sources rather than legal categories.

medium.set: Four surahs revealed entirely in the Makkan period
medium.explain: Surahs 6, 7, 10 and 12 are Makkan; the decoys are Madinan.

medium.set: Four of the Prophet's uncles
medium.explain: The decoys were companions, not relatives of that degree. Of the uncles listed, Hamza and al-Abbas accepted Islam.

hard.set: The six books of hadith (Kutub al-Sittah)
hard.explain: The six canonical Sunni hadith collections. Bukhari and Muslim are together known as the Sahihayn; the remaining four are the Sunan works.

hard.set: The four Sunni schools of jurisprudence
hard.explain: The four surviving Sunni madhhabs, named after Abu Hanifah, Malik ibn Anas, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

hard.set: The months of the Islamic year, 5th to 8th
hard.explain: The Islamic months in order are Muharram, Safar, Rabi al-Awwal, Rabi al-Thani, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhirah, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah.

hard.set: The surahs named after prophets
hard.explain: Six surahs carry the name of a prophet: Yunus (10), Hud (11), Yusuf (12), Ibrahim (14), Muhammad (47) and Nuh (71). Surah Maryam is named after a woman, not a prophet.

hard.set: The seven long surahs (al-Sab' al-Tiwal), first five
hard.explain: The seven long surahs begin the Qur'an after Al-Fatihah: Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma'idah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, and then either Al-Anfal with At-Tawbah together or Yunus, which scholars differ over.

hard.set: The compilers of the six books, in order of death
hard.explain: They died in this order between 870 and 915 CE. Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled the Muwatta and the Musnad, which are not among the six books.

hard.set: The seven long surahs (al-Sab' al-Tiwal), first six
hard.explain: The seventh is counted either as Al-Anfal with At-Tawbah together or as Yunus, a point on which scholars differ.

hard.set: The twelve Islamic months, the last four
hard.explain: The year ends with Ramadan (9), Shawwal (10), Dhul-Qa'dah (11) and Dhul-Hijjah (12).

hard.set: The Ulul-Azm prophets in chronological order
hard.explain: The five prophets of firm resolve, in the traditional chronological order in which they are usually listed.

hard.set: Surahs named after prophets, in mushaf order
hard.explain: Six surahs carry a prophet's name. Maryam is named after a woman who was not a prophet, Luqman after a wise man not generally counted a prophet, and Al-Anbiya means 'The Prophets' collectively.

hard.set: The four Rashidun caliphs with the years their rule began
hard.explain: The Rashidun period ran from 11 AH to 40 AH. Hasan ibn Ali's brief caliphate in 40 AH is counted by some as completing it.

hard.set: The founders of the four schools, in order of death
hard.explain: The four surviving Sunni schools, in the order their founders died. The decoys are real jurists whose schools did not survive as independent madhhabs.

hard.set: The surahs with a sajdah, first five in mushaf order
hard.explain: The verses of prostration are spread through the mushaf. The decoys also contain sajdahs but come later; scholars differ on the total count, commonly given as fourteen or fifteen.

hard.set: The first five surahs of juz 30, in order
hard.explain: Juz 30 begins at An-Naba and runs to An-Nas, thirty-seven surahs in all.

hard.set: The longest four surahs by verse count
hard.explain: By number of ayahs rather than length of text: Al-Baqarah 286, Ash-Shu'ara 227, Al-A'raf 206 and Al-Imran 200. Counting by words gives a different ordering.

hard.set: The twelve Islamic months, the first six
hard.explain: The first half of the Islamic year. The decoys are months seven to ten.

hard.set: The six books with their compilers
hard.explain: The six canonical collections. The decoys are major collections that fall outside the six.

hard.set: The four school founders with their years of death
hard.explain: The decoys are genuine jurists of the same era whose schools did not survive as independent madhhabs.

hard.set: The longest five surahs by verse count
hard.explain: Ranked by number of ayahs rather than length of text. By word count the ordering differs considerably, since many later surahs have shorter verses.

hard.set: The surahs numbered 20 to 24, in order
hard.explain: Surahs 20 to 24. Maryam is 19 and Al-Furqan is 25, immediately either side.

hard.set: The disconnected-letter openings of five surahs
hard.explain: Twenty-nine surahs open with disconnected letters. Most scholars hold their meaning to be known to Allah alone.

hard.set: The Rashidun caliphs' approximate lengths of rule
decoys: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz — about 2 years
hard.explain: The four Rashidun caliphates spanned roughly 11 to 40 AH. Hasan's brief rule is counted by some as completing the period.

hard.set: Five surahs containing a verse of prostration, in mushaf order
hard.explain: None of the four long surahs offered as decoys contains a sajdah. Scholars differ on the total count, commonly given as fourteen or fifteen.

hard.set: Surahs named after prophets, with their numbers
hard.explain: Six surahs carry a prophet's name. Maryam is named after a woman, Luqman after a sage not generally counted a prophet, and Al-Anbiya means 'The Prophets' collectively.

hard.set: The eight categories entitled to zakat, in Qur'anic order
hard.explain: The eight categories are listed in Surah At-Tawbah 9:60. One may not give obligatory zakat to those one is already required to maintain, such as parents or children.

hard.set: The compilers of the six books, with the regions they are associated with
hard.explain: Five of the six compilers take their names from places in Khurasan and Transoxiana. The decoys are the school founders and their centres.

hard.set: The first five surahs after Al-Fatihah, with verse counts
hard.explain: Surahs 2 to 6. Note that Al-Ma'idah, at 120, is shorter by verse count than Al-An'am, which follows it.

hard.set: The main rites of Hajj in order, five of them
hard.explain: The core sequence of Hajj days. Tawaf al-Wada is the farewell circumambulation performed last, and visiting Madinah is not a rite of Hajj at all.

hard.set: Five of the Asma al-Husna with their meanings
hard.explain: The first five names in the traditional enumeration, in the order they are usually listed. The decoys are also among the ninety-nine but come later.

hard.set: Five surahs revealed in Madinah
hard.explain: Surahs 2 to 5 and 8 are Madinan. The decoys, surahs 6, 7, 10 and 11, are Makkan. Classification is by period rather than strictly by place.

hard.set: The twelve Islamic months, the last six
hard.explain: Months seven to twelve. The decoys are from the first half of the year.

hard.set: The Ten Promised Paradise, the last six
hard.explain: The first four of the ten are the Rashidun caliphs. The decoys are eminent companions not named in that narration.

hard.set: Surahs 25 to 29, in order
hard.explain: Surahs 25 to 29. An-Nur is 24, immediately before, and Ar-Rum is 30, immediately after.

hard.set: Surahs 30 to 34, in order
hard.explain: Surahs 30 to 34. Fatir is 35 and Yasin 36, which follow.

hard.set: The three surahs with exactly three ayahs
hard.explain: Only three surahs have exactly three ayahs: Al-Asr (103), Al-Kawthar (108) and An-Nasr (110). Al-Ikhlas and Quraysh have four, and Al-Fil and Al-Falaq five.

hard.set: The four caliphs and the manner of the end of their rule
decoys: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz — died in office
hard.explain: Three of the four Rashidun caliphs were killed. Hasan ibn Ali, by contrast, ceded authority rather than being removed by force.

hard.set: Six of the Asma al-Husna in their traditional order, positions 6 to 11
hard.explain: The traditional enumeration opens Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim, Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, then those listed here. The decoys are the earlier names.

hard.set: Five Makkan surahs among the first twenty
hard.explain: Surahs 6, 7, 10, 11 and 12 are Makkan, while the decoys — surahs 2 to 5 — are Madinan.

hard.set: The six books in the order they are conventionally listed
hard.explain: The conventional listing places the two Sahihs first, then the four Sunan works. Some scholars substitute the Muwatta for Ibn Majah in the sixth position.

hard.set: Four events of 8 AH, in order
hard.explain: Four events fall within 8 AH alone. The decoys belong to 6, 7, 9 and 10 AH respectively.

hard.set: Five prophets named in Surah Al-An'am's list, in the order given
hard.explain: Surah Al-An'am 6:83–86 lists a sequence of prophets. The decoys also appear in that passage, but later in it.

hard.set: The approximate death years of five major mufassirun and historians
hard.explain: The decoys are hadith compilers and jurists of earlier centuries rather than the later exegetes and scholars listed.

hard.set: Five surahs whose names are single Arabic letters or letter combinations
hard.explain: Several surahs take their names from the disconnected letters that open them. Surah Al-Qalam opens with the letter Nun.

hard.set: Five of the surahs revealed earliest, by common accounts
hard.explain: The earliest revelations are generally held to include these. The decoys are Madinan surahs revealed much later. Orderings of revelation differ between scholars.

hard.set: Five surahs placed between 60 and 66 in the mushaf
hard.explain: Surahs 60 to 64. Al-Hashr is 59, At-Talaq 65, At-Tahrim 66 and Al-Mulk 67.

hard.set: Five surahs opening with 'Alhamdulillah'
hard.explain: Exactly five surahs open with praise of Allah: Al-Fatihah (1), Al-An'am (6), Al-Kahf (18), Saba (34) and Fatir (35).

hard.set: The Musabbihat — surahs opening with glorification of Allah
hard.explain: The Musabbihat are the surahs opening with a form of tasbih, glorification of Allah. Different scholars count them slightly differently.

hard.set: Surahs 35 to 39, in order
hard.explain: Surahs 35 to 39. Saba is 34, just before; Ghafir is 40, just after.

hard.set: Surahs 40 to 44, in order
hard.explain: Surahs 40 to 44, the group often called the Hawamim for their shared opening letters. The decoys are surahs 45 to 48.

hard.set: Five companions appointed governors during the Rashidun period
hard.explain: Each of the five held a genuine appointment. The decoys pair real companions with posts they did not hold.

hard.set: Five of the Prophet's wives after Khadijah
hard.explain: The decoys are the Prophet's daughters. Note that Zaynab bint Jahsh, a wife, and Zaynab bint Muhammad, a daughter, share a name.

hard.set: The four surahs with exactly five ayahs
hard.explain: Al-Qadr (97), Al-Fil (105), Al-Masad (111) and Al-Falaq (113) each have five ayahs. Al-Ikhlas and Quraysh have four, and Al-Asr and Al-Kawthar three.

hard.set: Five of the ten promised Paradise who were not caliphs
hard.explain: Six of the ten were not caliphs; Sa'id ibn Zayd is the sixth. The decoys are eminent companions not named in that narration.

hard.set: Five surahs placed between 85 and 90 in the mushaf
hard.explain: Surahs 85 to 89. Al-Balad is 90, Ash-Shams 91, Al-Layl 92 and Ad-Duha 93.

hard.set: Five surahs placed between 90 and 95 in the mushaf
hard.explain: Surahs 90 to 94. At-Tin is 95, Al-Alaq 96, Al-Qadr 97 and Al-Bayyinah 98.

hard.set: Five early Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia
hard.explain: The decoys remained in Makkah with the Prophet ﷺ rather than joining the migration to Abyssinia.

hard.set: Five scholars and the works they are best known for
hard.explain: The decoys deliberately mismatch scholars with works by others.

hard.set: Five battles of the Rashidun period, in order
hard.explain: The decoys all took place during the Prophet's lifetime, before the Rashidun period began.

hard.set: Five of the Asma al-Husna concerning forgiveness and mercy
hard.explain: The names listed concern mercy and forgiveness; the decoys concern might, compelling power and justice.

hard.set: Five surahs of juz 30 with more than twenty ayahs
hard.explain: The longer surahs of juz 30 cluster at its start; the very short ones come near the end of the mushaf.
